summary: A developer blog you own: Markdown posts in a repo rendered by Astro with syntax highlighting, tags, RSS, search and a generated OG image per post, deployed to your domain, with a script that cross-posts to Hashnode with the canonical URL pointing home so you keep the feed without giving up ownership.

stack.choice: Astro with content collections, static output
stack.why: validated frontmatter and zero client JavaScript by default

stack.choice: Markdown and MDX files in the repo
stack.why: the folder is the CMS and git is the history

stack.choice: Any static host on your domain

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your existing posts exported
prerequisites.why: Phase 1 imports them with their original dates.
prerequisites.get: Hashnode: Blog dashboard > Export > download the JSON or Markdown export.

prerequisites.name: A static host connected to the repo
prerequisites.get: Cloudflare Pages or Netlify: connect the repository, build command npm run build, output dist.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: Your posts at your address; canonical points here.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: A Hashnode personal access token (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 6 cross-posts via the API with canonical set to your domain.
prerequisites.get: Hashnode > Account settings > Developer > Generate new token.

env.name: HASHNODE_TOKEN
env.where: Developer token for cross-posting. Empty disables the script.

env.name: HASHNODE_PUBLICATION_ID
env.where: From your Hashnode blog dashboard URL or the API.

phases.title: Posts and routing
phases.goal: A validated content collection, post pages, an index, drafts excluded, code highlighted at build time.

steps.do: Create the Astro project and the posts collection with a frontmatter schema
steps.detail: title, date, slug, tags, description, canonical (optional), draft.
commands: npm create astro@latest blog -- --template minimal --typescript strict --install --git

steps.do: Import the export into Markdown files with original dates; add /:slug and an index sorted by date

check: A post with a missing title fails the build naming the file
A draft is absent from the build
A code block renders highlighted with zero JavaScript shipped

phases.title: Reading experience
phases.goal: Typography, dark mode, a table of contents, reading time, anchors.

steps.do: Build the post layout with a measured line length and system fonts
Generate a table of contents from headings, add reading time and heading anchors

check: A long post is readable on a phone without horizontal scroll from a code block

phases.title: Tags, RSS and search
phases.goal: Tag pages, a full-content feed, a sitemap, small client-side search.

steps.do: Add /tags/:tag, RSS with full content and a sitemap
Build a search JSON index at build time under 50 kB and a small search box

check: Every tag page lists the right posts
Search finds a post by a word in its description

phases.title: SEO and cards
phases.goal: Canonical honoured, OG and JSON-LD present, an OG image per post.

steps.do: Add canonical from frontmatter or SITE_URL, Open Graph, Twitter meta and JSON-LD Article
Generate a 1200x630 OG image per post at build time with satori and resvg

check: A post previews correctly in a card validator
Canonical points where the frontmatter says

phases.title: Newsletter signup
phases.goal: Emails stored locally; no sending in v1.

steps.do: One small Node endpoint storing to SQLite with honeypot and rate limit
A form on every post and a CSV export

check: A signup stores once; a duplicate is a no-op
The CSV opens in a spreadsheet

phases.title: Deploy and cross-post
phases.goal: Live on your domain, mirrored on Hashnode with canonical home.

steps.do: Connect the static host and the custom domain
Write scripts/crosspost.mjs that publishes a post to Hashnode via its GraphQL API with canonicalUrl set
steps.detail: Publish here first, syndicate second; the reverse leaves Hashnode canonical.

check: A new post is live on your domain
The mirror on Hashnode has canonical pointing home, verified in the page source

phases.title: Operate the newsletter endpoint
phases.goal: Only if you keep the signup: monitor and back it up like any small server.

steps.do: Nightly backup of the signups database off the box and one restore

check: An alert fires when the endpoint is stopped

product.outcome: A blog that is yours by default and still reaches the Hashnode audience by syndication.

architecture.swap: Another static generator against the same files
Add Medium or dev.to with the same canonical rule

operations.backup: The repo is the backup; the signup database nightly.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on the site and the endpoint.
operations.incident: A bad deploy is reverted with git.

releaseGate: Canonical verified on a mirrored post
One restore of the signup database

notIncluded: The network feed; cross-posting with canonical is the honest way to keep it.
after: Cross-post to dev.to with the same canonical rule
A series or collection page type
